services.name: Gwanda Agro Supplies
services.notes: Main agro dealer for Gwanda district and the provincial capital area. Primary focus is livestock inputs — Gwanda is cattle country. Seed range limited to drought-tolerant varieties: SC403 short-season maize, SDMV millet, sorghum. Order specialised inputs from Bulawayo.

services.name: Plumtree Agro Dealer — Bulilima
services.notes: Plumtree is on the Zimbabwe–Botswana border — some cross-border trade in inputs. Cotton seed from Quton available through Cottco contract for the Bulilima communal cotton belt. Small grain varieties for the very dry conditions. Botswana traders sometimes bring inputs across — compare prices.

services.name: Esigodini Agro Inputs — Umzingwane
services.notes: Umzingwane is the most productive district in Matabeleland South — proximity to Bulawayo and better rainfall. Maize, groundnuts, and vegetables more viable here. Esigodini market gardeners supply Bulawayo with vegetables.

services.name: GMB — Gwanda Depot
services.notes: GMB Gwanda — the only significant GMB depot in Matabeleland South. Accepts sorghum, millet, maize, groundnuts. Volumes are very low in most years due to erratic rainfall. The depot is also used for emergency food distribution. Register seller number early even if you expect a small harvest.

services.name: Gwanda Town Market
services.notes: Gwanda town market. Mine workers from Blanket Gold Mine are an important market. Fresh vegetables mostly trucked in from Bulawayo. Local sorghum, groundnuts, and tropical fruit sold when available. Limited local production — most farmers are subsistence-level.

services.name: Beitbridge Border Market
services.notes: Beitbridge is Zimbabwe's busiest border crossing to South Africa. A unique market opportunity — cross-border traders buy Zimbabwean produce and bring South African goods back. Citrus, tomatoes, and tropical fruit sell at the border. NOTE: Beitbridge district is technically Matabeleland South but borders Mwenezi (Masvingo). Market serves both provinces.

services.name: Esigodini Fresh Market — Umzingwane
services.notes: Roadside market on the Harare–Bulawayo highway. Esigodini market gardeners sell vegetables to passing travellers — similar to Norton in Mashonaland West. Good prices for covo, tomatoes, and carrots during season. Convenient access to Bulawayo buyers.

services.name: Gwanda Livestock Auction
services.open_hours: Monthly auction — last Wednesday of month
services.notes: Main cattle auction for Matabeleland South. Cattle from Gwanda, Matobo, Insiza, and Bulilima districts. Monthly sales. Cross-border cattle trade with Botswana and South Africa significant — Gwanda cattle well-known in regional markets. Bring veterinary movement permits.

services.name: Cottco — Insiza and Bulilima Cotton Buying
services.notes: Cotton buying for Insiza and Bulilima districts. Cotton in Matabeleland South requires careful variety selection — drought-tolerant Bt varieties recommended for this rainfall zone. Bulilima cotton near Plumtree border has some unique micro-climates. Grade S1 required for best price. Quton seed on Cottco credit contract.

services.name: AGRITEX Provincial Office — Matabeleland South
services.notes: Provincial AGRITEX HQ for Matabeleland South. Coordinates 6 district offices. The primary mandate in this province is food security — drought-resilient crop promotion, livestock management, and Conservation Agriculture. Government emergency input schemes are managed from this office.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Bulilima (Plumtree)
services.notes: Bulilima is the westernmost district, bordering Botswana. Dry — sorghum and millet dominant. Cotton grown in better areas. Some cross-border agricultural information exchange with Botswana — ward officers have awareness of regional seed varieties.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Insiza (Filabusi)
services.notes: Insiza has slightly better rainfall than Gwanda and Bulilima — some cotton and maize viable. Ward officers advise on Cottco contract registration and drought-tolerant maize. Conservation Agriculture promoted extensively here.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Mangwe
services.address: District Agricultural Office, Mangwe Growth Point
services.notes: Mangwe is one of Zimbabwe's driest districts — Region 5. Cattle and goats are the primary livelihood. Very limited arable farming — sorghum and millet only in the wettest years. Moringa for nutrition being promoted. Emergency food assistance is a regular feature of this district.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Matobo (Kezi)
services.notes: Matobo is a rocky district — the famous Matobo Hills and national park. Farming on rocky, thin soils is challenging. Ward officers advise on soil conservation on slopes. Sorghum and maize in valley bottoms (dambo areas) where soils are deeper.

services.name: AGRITEX District Office — Umzingwane (Esigodini)
services.notes: Umzingwane is the most agriculturally active district in Matabeleland South — proximity to Bulawayo, good road, and slightly higher rainfall. Ward officers advise on vegetable production for Bulawayo market. Irrigation along Umzingwane River supports market gardening.

services.name: Matopos Research Station
services.address: Matopos Research Station, 35 km south of Bulawayo on Matobo Road
services.notes: National research station — the most important agricultural research centre for dryland semi-arid farming in Zimbabwe. Primary focus: drought-tolerant sorghum, pearl millet, groundnuts, cowpeas, bambara groundnut (nyimo), and lablab. Pasture research for livestock. Annual field day — essential for all Matabeleland farmers. Certified seed of improved small grain varieties available from this station.

services.name: Agribank Zimbabwe — Gwanda Branch
services.notes: Agribank Gwanda. Agricultural lending is limited by the harsh farming environment. Primary products: livestock loans for cattle ranchers, crop loans for Umzingwane and Insiza where farming is more viable. Cotton input loans through Cottco for registered contract farmers. Larger facilities handled through Bulawayo branch.

services.name: Matabeleland South Community Seed Bank — Matobo
services.notes: Community seed bank holding locally-adapted varieties for the Matobo hills area — varieties developed over generations for the specific rocky soil and erratic rainfall conditions. Drought-tolerant sorghum, pearl millet, nyimo beans, and cowpeas. Access through AGRITEX Matobo. Seed is shared under a community agreement — borrowers return double at harvest. More reliable than commercial channels for these microclimate-adapted varieties.
